title: Electricity "disconnection tonight" to a personal UPI ID vs. due-date reminder
summary: A caller from Deccan Power Distribution phones about the recipient's electricity bill. In the fraud case, the caller says power will be cut tonight and tells the recipient to pay immediately to a personal UPI ID that the caller reads out. In the legitimate case, the caller reminds the recipient that the bill is due soon and lists the official payment channels, all of which use the recipient's consumer number. Both callers mention UPI and possible disconnection.

shared_setting.pretext: the latest bill of [AMOUNT_1] (₹800–₹6,000) is unpaid.
shared_setting.recipient_profile: an adult household account holder; age, occupation, and city sampled at generation.
other_facts: Both callers mention that unpaid bills can lead to disconnection and that the bill can be paid by UPI.

fraud.label_rationale: The caller demands payment to an individual's UPI ID, not through any of the company's billing channels, and uses a same-night deadline to force it.
fraud.caller_objective: Get the recipient to send [AMOUNT_1] or more to [UPI_ID_1].
stable_facts: [UPI_ID_1] is a personal-looking handle. The caller calls it "the officer's ID" or "the department's direct ID".
Deadline: supply will be cut "tonight" or "within two hours".
The caller may quote the consumer number or the bill amount. Neither proves legitimacy.

legitimate.label_rationale: The caller reminds the recipient of an upcoming due date and points only to official billing channels tied to the consumer number. No payment is taken on the call and no personal account is mentioned.
legitimate.caller_objective: Get the bill paid by the due date.
stable_facts: Due date: five to ten days away.
Channels: the Deccan Power app or website (typed by the recipient), the bill-payment section of any UPI or banking app using the consumer number, or a Deccan Power collection counter.
The caller says a late fee may apply after the due date and that disconnection happens only after a written notice.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud caller may repeat the UPI ID, add urgency, or claim the crew is already on the way. They must not switch to a different mechanism (for example a link, app install, or OTP). The legitimate caller must not name any personal payee or take payment details after the branch.

must_preserve: bill amount and "unpaid" framing in both
personal UPI ID and same-night deadline (_F)
official consumer-number channels and "only after written notice" (_L)
may_vary: whether the recipient believes they already paid
up to 2 filler turns before turn 3

ambiguities: UPI", "disconnection", and "pay today" can appear in both cases. The label depends on the payee: an individual UPI ID versus the utility's own billing channels.

Real fraud of this type often begins with an SMS asking the consumer to call an "officer". This family uses an outbound call so the pair shares a channel. An SMS-first variant would be a separate family.
A legitimate utility may send payment links by official SMS. The legitimate caller here sends none, so a link is not a confound in this pair.
The recipient's belief that they already paid is not evidence either way.

evidence_references.claim: Disconnection for non-payment requires at least fifteen clear days' written notice (CB07)
Disconnection tonight, call the officer" messages are fake per PIB Fact Check (CB08)
Impostors cite a penalty or urgency to extract payment or credentials (C02)
Fraud can be reported on 1930 / cybercrime.gov.in (C12)
